data.text: Fix ddflow bug B45d5aa72fa via item B-fix-import-done-phases: import --include-done must complete finished phases (with evidence), re-run must add missing ticked tasks under existing phases idempotently without touching human-changed items, plain import must report ticked tasks left out; regression test tests/test_import_done_phases.py; dry-run on run_nemo_run without --apply.

data.claim: plan_import skips any id already in state (f.ident in known -> skipped_existing) and apply_import writes phase.added only, never a phase completion; tasks re-run under an existing phase land with parent=phase id because scan ids are stable. With include_done every phase of the fixture imports open; a plain import brings in a finished phase that open work needs (P5) EMPTY and OPEN, so its dependent is stuck.
data.falsifier: Any phase in the fixture's --include-done plan with done=True, or a completion written for an existing phase on re-run.
data.probe: uv run pytest tests/test_import_done_phases.py (new regression test) against unfixed main code
data.probe_output: 5 failed, 1 passed: include-done plan phases {'1': False, '2': False, '3': False, 'P5': False}; re-run completions set() != {'P5'}; plain note says 'pass include_done' but never '--include-done' nor per-phase counts
data.question: Does the importer ever complete a phase, and how does a re-run decide 'already in the queue, left alone'?

evidence.note: R6e696bd22c CONFIRMED: probe = new regression test on unfixed code, 5 failed/1 passed; importer never writes a phase completion; re-run left-alone is id-in-known

ran brief --item and recall: binding decision on local services (not touched by this change); lessons L-import-read-against-handoff (check held/dropped items against the handoff), L07ad0f5dd2 (descriptive ids); memory Mcbce75696a (pin PYTHONPATH for main vs worktree code)

commit f639a8e: _settle_phases/_phase_verdict decide phase completion after tasks are in the plan; completion kind for existing imported phases; touched_since_import from the log; per-phase ticked-left-out note + apply count; tests/test_import_done_phases.py 8 passed, import suites 106 passed

data.summary: A plain 'ddflow import --apply' (no --include-done) keeps a finished phase that open work depends on (plan_import: live_phases |= needs) but imports it EMPTY and OPEN, since its ticked tasks are left out -- so the dependent is never offered. Probe: '## Phase 3' with '- [ ] **3.B** Needs: P5' and '## P5' with two '- [x]' boxes -> import --apply; ddflow next exits 2: '3.B: deps -- phase P5 has no open tasks but is not marked done'. --include-done completes P5 after B-fix-import-done-phases; the plain path should complete such a phase too (evidence: every box under it ticked) or pull its ticked tasks in as done, like _pull_in_needed does for tasks.

data.rule: When a re-run of an importer may complete or alter an item already in the queue, decide 'untouched since import' from the event log (every event on the subject was the importer's own), and decide a child's done-ness by who set its CURRENT state. The folded state cannot tell open-because-untouched from open-because-reopened. Also run 'python -m ddflow' from a neutral cwd when testing a worktree: -m puts cwd first on sys.path, so running from the primary checkout silently uses main's code.
data.title: An import that may change existing items must read provenance from the log, not the fold
